αἰπὺ: αἰπύς — steep, sheer; adj., neut. acc. sg., agreeing with ὄρος · also with other neut. nouns (αἰπὺ πτολίεθρον ’steep citadel’)
αἱ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. pl. ’they’, referring to the ships (αἱ δ’ ... ἔπλεον) · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of women (αἱ δ’ ὅτε ... ἵκοντο ’and when they came’) · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the mules (αἱ δ’ ὦκα λίπον ’and they quickly left’) · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the islands (αἱ δέ τ’ ἄνευθε ’and they lie apart’)
αἴθοπα: αἴθοψ — fire-faced, sparkling (of wine, lit. αἴθω ’burn’ + ὤψ ’face’); masc. acc. sg.
αἶψ: αἶψα — quickly, swiftly; adv., elided (αἶψ’ = αἶψα)
αὐδήεσσα: αὐδήεις — endowed with speech or voice (from αὐδή); anciently explained as ’speaking with a human voice’, exact force debated; fem. nom. sg.
αὐτήν: αὐτός — self; intensive/personal pron., fem. acc. sg.: ’her, it’
αὐτίχ: αὐτίκα — at once, straightaway; adv., elided and aspirated before a rough breathing (αὐτίχ’ = αὐτίκα)
αὐτοῦ: αὐτός — self; masc. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive (ἑὸν αὐτοῦ ’his own very own’): ’of himself’ · also the fixed adv. αὐτοῦ, ’there, on the spot, right here’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun, unemphatic ’him’, governed by a preposition: ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ’from him’ · also intensive with a noun, masc. gen. sg.: ’Alcinous himself’ (αὐτοῦ Ἀλκινόοιο)
αὐτόθ: αὐτόθι — right there, on the spot; adv., elided (αὐτόθ’ = αὐτόθι)
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὐτὴν: αὐτός — self; fem. acc. sg.: ’her’ · also intensive, accusative subject of an infinitive: ’she herself’ (αὐτὴν ποθέσαι ’that she herself miss [him]’) · also attributive, ’the same’: τῷ αὐτὴν ὁδὸν ’the very same road’
αὐτῷ: αὐτός — self; masc. dat. sg.: ’himself’, reinforcing a personal pronoun (σοὶ δ’ αὐτῷ ’to you yourself’) · also used alone as a plain personal pronoun, ’him’, not reinforcing anything (ἐπ’ αὐτῷ μηχανόωνται ’are plotting against him’) · also with a noun, ’own, very’, in the dat. of accompaniment: αὐτῷ φάρει ’with the cloak itself, cloak and all’ · also reinforcing a 1st-person pronoun: ’myself’ (ἐμοὶ αὐτῷ)
αὖθι: αὖθι — there, on the spot, right there; adv.
βάλλον: βάλλω — throw, cast; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented (= Attic ἔβαλλον): ’were casting, threw’
βαρέα: βαρύς — heavy, grievous; adj., neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’heavily’ (βαρέα στενάχοντα ’groaning heavily’)
βοὴν: βοή — shout, war-cry; fem. acc. sg. of respect: ‘good at the war-cry’ (βοὴν ἀγαθός)
βοῶν: βοῦς — ox, cow; pl. ’cattle’; gen. pl.
βῆν: βαίνω — go, step; aor. 1 sg., unaugmented (= ἔβην)
γ: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle (elided γ’)
γαίῃ: γαῖα — earth, ground; fem. dat. sg.
γαλήνη: γαλήνη — calm (of the sea); fem. nom. sg.
δέδεντο: δέω — bind, tie; plpf. pass. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ἐδέδεντο): ’had been tied, were tied’
δείσαντες: δείδω — fear, dread; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having feared’
δεινὴ: δεινός — dread, terrible, awesome; fem. nom. sg.
δεῖπνον: δεῖπνον — meal, supper; neut. acc. sg. (περὶ δεῖπνον ’about the meal’)
διὰ: διά — through, throughout; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: διὰ … τινάξῃ = διατινάξῃ ’shake apart, shatter’ · also + acc., causal, ’through, thanks to, by the aid of’ (διὰ … Ἀθήνην) · also as adverb/preverb in tmesis with κοσμηθέντες (διὰ … κοσμηθέντες = διακοσμηθέντες ’drawn up in divisions’) · also + gen., ’through, among’ (διὰ μήλων ’among the flocks’)
δοάσσατο: δοάσσατο — it seemed; rare aor. 3 sg. (lemma disputed, akin to δοκέω), impersonal
δοιοὺς: δοιοί — two (poetic alternative to δύο); numeral adj., masc. acc. pl.
δόμεναι: δίδωμι — give; aor. inf., epic -μεναι, used as imperative: ’give’ · also inf. after ὀτρύνω, ’to give’ (πομπὴν ὀτρύνω δόμεναι ’I urge (him) to give a conveyance’)
δόρυ: δόρυ — wood, tree-trunk, timber; also spear; neut. nom. sg.
δύω: δύο — two; numeral, epic by-form δύω, indeclinable
δώματα: δῶμα — house, dwelling; neut. acc. pl. (plural for a single dwelling): ’house, home’
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῶ: δῶ — house, home; indeclinable epic noun (= δῶμα), used as nom./acc. sg. · also δίδωμι ’give’: aor. subj. 1 sg., ’I may give’ (ἵνα τοι δῶ ’that I may give you’)
εἰπὼν: εἶπον — say, speak; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.
εἰς: εἰς — into, to; prep. + acc. · also εἰμί ’be’: pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic εἶ): ’you are’ (τίς … εἰς; ’who are you?’) · also in the idiom εἰς ὅ (κε) ’until’: εἰς ὅ κεν … μιγήῃς ’until you mingle with’
εἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. (accented εἴ before a following enclitic, περ among them) · also introducing an indirect question, ‘whether’ (τίς δ’ οἶδ’ εἴ κέ ... ‘who knows whether’) · also with opt., of an aim in view: ’in case, to see if’ (εἴ τινά … λάβοι ’in case he might catch someone’)
εἴη: εἰμί — be; pres. opt. 3 sg.: ’it might be, he might be’; impersonal + inf.: ’it might be possible for him’
εἶεν: εἰμί — be; pres. opt. 3 pl., in an indirect question: ’(who) they might be’ · also with κε, potential: ’would be’ (κ’ … εἶεν)
εὐρυοδείης: εὐρυόδεια — wide-wayed (fem. adj., of the earth); fem. gen. sg.
εὗρον: εὑρίσκω — find; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ηὗρον)
θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — and; connective particle
θανάτοιο: θάνατος — death; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θεὸς: θεός — god; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’as a god’ · also plain nom. sg. subject, an unspecified deity left unnamed: ’a god’ (θεὸς δ’ ἐκέδασσεν Ἀχαιούς ’a god scattered the Achaeans’) · also of a goddess (θεός is common gender)
θοὴν: θοός — swift, quick; fem. acc. sg.
θυμός: θυμός — heart, spirit; masc. nom. sg.
θυμὸν: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; acc. sg.
θυμὸς: θυμός — heart, spirit, desire; nom. sg.
θῖνα: θίς — shore, beach; fem. acc. sg.
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κέρδιον: κερδίων — more profitable, better; neut. nom. sg., comparative of κέρδος
κήρυχ: κῆρυξ — herald; masc. acc. sg., elided (κήρυχ’ = κήρυκα)
κίρκη: Κίρκη — Circe, the enchantress goddess; fem. nom. sg.
κακότητα: κακότης — badness, misery, trouble; fem. acc. sg.
κακὸς: κακός — bad, base, cowardly; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’base’ · also masc. nom. sg., attributive with a noun: ’evil’ (κακὸς δαίμων ’an evil power’)
καμάτῳ: κάματος — toil, weariness; masc. dat. sg.
καρπαλίμως: καρπάλιμος — swift, nimble; adv. καρπαλίμως: ’swiftly, nimbly’
κατ: κατά (elided κατ’) — down from, throughout; + gen./acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (κατ’ … ἕζετο = κατέζετο ’sat down’)
κατεβήσετο: καταβαίνω — go down, descend; aor. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= κατέβη)
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’) · also ’according to, in conformity with’ (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’) · also + acc., ’in quest of, after’ (κατὰ ληίδα ’in quest of plunder’) · also + gen., ’down from’ (κατὰ πετράων ’down from the rocks’) · also + gen., ’all over, throughout’ (κατὰ σπείους κέχυτο ’lay spread all over the cave’) · also + acc., of the part grasped: ’by’ (κατὰ νῶτα λαβών ’taking him by the back’)
κείμεθ: κεῖμαι — lie; impf. 1 pl., unaugmented, elided (κείμεθ’ = κείμεθα): ’we lay’
κιὼν: κίω — go; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’going’
κλυτὰ: κλυτός — famous, renowned; neut. nom./acc. pl.
κλυτὸν: κλυτός — famous, renowned, glorious; masc. acc. sg.
κούρῃ: κούρη — girl, maiden, daughter (Attic κόρη); dat. sg.
κρίνας: κρίνω — pick out, choose, judge; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having picked out’
κυανοπρῴροιο: κυανόπρῳρος — dark-prowed; gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), with νεός
κώπῃς: κώπη — oar; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃς (= Attic κώπαις): ’with oars’
κὰδ: κατά (apocope κάδ before δ-) — down through, throughout; prep./preverb in tmesis: ’throughout the halls’ (κὰδ δώματα = κατὰ δώματα) · also a bare preverb in tmesis with a verb: κὰδ ... ἔβαλε = κατέβαλε ’threw down’
λευκὴ: λευκός — white, bright; fem. nom. sg.
λυγρὸν: λυγρός — baneful, bitter, grievous; masc. acc. sg.
μάλ: μάλα (elided μάλ’) — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάρψας: μάρπτω — seize, grab; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having seized’
μέγ: μέγας — great; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially, elided (μέγ’ = μέγα): ’greatly’ · also plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. noun, not adverbial: κῦμα μέγ’ ’a great wave’
μέγα: μέγας — great, huge; neut. nom./acc. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’greatly’ (μέγα νήπιοι ’greatly foolish’)
μέγαν: μέγας — great, big, tall; masc. acc. sg.
μέλαιναν: μέλας — black, dark; fem. acc. sg., agreeing with κῆρα · also agreeing with νῆα (θοὴν ἀνὰ νῆα μέλαιναν ’the swift black ship’)
μένος: μένος — force, might, spirit, drive; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject (μένος … ἐνέστακται ’his force has been instilled’)
μεγάροισι: μέγαρον — hall; dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
μειλιχίοις: μειλίχιος — gentle, soothing; masc. dat. pl., with ἐπέεσσιν
μερμήριξα: μερμηρίζω — ponder, be torn in mind; aor. 1 sg.
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’
μυρίοι: μυρίος — countless, numberless; masc. nom. pl. (later ’ten thousand’)
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μῆλα: μῆλον — sheep, goat, flock-animal; neut. nom. pl.: ’the flocks’ · also neut. acc. pl. (same form), direct object: ἦγον ... μῆλα ’they led sheep’
νέας: ναῦς — ship; fem. acc. pl., epic νέας (= Attic ναῦς)
νεὸς: ναῦς — ship; fem. gen. sg., epic-Ionic (= Attic νεώς)
νηὸς: ναῦς — ship; gen. sg., epic νηός (= Attic νεώς)
νηῦς: ναῦς — ship; nom. sg., epic νηῦς
νηῶν: ναῦς — ship; fem. gen. pl., epic νηῶν (= Attic νεῶν)
νομεύων: νομεύω — pasture, tend (flocks); pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’tending’
νύκτας: νύξ — night; fem. acc. pl., acc. of time: ’by nights’
νῆα: ναῦς — ship; acc. sg., epic νῆα
νῆας: ναῦς — ship; fem. acc. pl., epic νῆας (= Attic ναῦς)
νῶτα: νῶτον — back; neut. acc. pl. νῶτα, poetic image ’the broad back(s) of the sea’ · also ’back’ of a person: ’his back’ (ἥ οἱ νῶτα … ἄμπεχεν) · also the backs of animals: ’backs’ (ὀίων … νῶτα)
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’) · also encl. dat. sg. fem. ’to/for her’ (ἥ οἱ ὁμηλικίη ’who was of an age with her’)
οἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl. · also encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (= οἱ, accented οἵ in this position) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; masc. nom. pl. ’they’, demonstrative: οἵ γ’ ὑβρισταί ’are they violent?’
οἶον: οἶος — alone, only; masc. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., agreeing with the subject: ’standing alone’ (ὅ τε φαίνεται οἶον ’which appears alone’)
οἶος: οἶος — alone, only; masc. nom. sg.
οἷσιν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; possessive adj., neut./masc. dat. pl. (ν-movable): ’his own’ (agreeing with δώμασιν) · also relative, masc./neut. dat. pl.: whom (λαῶν οἷσιν ἄνασσε), not the possessive
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)
οὐκέτι: οὐκέτι — no longer, not any more; adv.
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὔτ: οὔτε (elided οὔτ’) — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
οὔτε: οὔτε — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
πάντες: πᾶς — all, every; masc. nom. pl.
πέρι: περί — around, about, exceedingly; adv. with anastrophe (accent thrown back): ’beyond all others’ (πέρι κέρδεα οἶδεν) · also preposition with anastrophe + acc., of place: ’around’ (ἄστυ πέρι ’around the city’)
πέτρη: πέτρη — rock, crag; fem. nom. sg.
παρὰ: παρά — beside, along, from; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · also used as an adverb with no case expressed: ’beside, alongside’ (παρὰ … ἐτάνυσσε τράπεζαν ’drew a table up beside (them)’)
παῖδα: παῖς — child, son, daughter; masc./fem. acc. sg.
πείσματα: πεῖσμα — ship’s cable, mooring rope; neut. acc. pl.
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’ · also after εἰ, ’if indeed, even if’: εἴ περ γάρ κεν ’if indeed ever’
πετράων: πέτρη — rock; fem. gen. pl., epic (πετράων = Attic πετρῶν)
πεύθεσθαι: πυνθάνομαι — learn, inquire; pres. inf., epic πεύθομαι (= Attic πυνθάνεσθαι): ’to find out’
πλέομεν: πλέω — sail; pres. 1 pl., vivid narrative present for a past situation: ‘we were sailing’
πλησίαι: πλήσιος — near, close; fem. nom. pl., + gen.: ’close to one another’ (πλησίαι ἀλλήλων)
ποιμένα: ποιμήν — shepherd; masc. acc. sg. (ποιμένα λαῶν ’shepherd of the people’, apposition)
ποιμὴν: ποιμήν — shepherd, herdsman; masc. nom. sg.
πολυβενθέος: πολυβενθής — very deep, many-fathomed (πολύς + βένθος); adj., fem. gen. sg.
ποτ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; enclitic adv., elided (ποτ’ = ποτέ)
προΐειν: προΐημι — send forth; impf. 1 sg., epic (= Attic προΐην): ’I sent forward’
προβλῆτες: προβλής — jutting out, projecting; adj., fem. nom. pl. (of a rocky shoreline)
προπάροιθε: προπάροιθε — before, in front of; adv./prep. + gen.
προτέρω: πρότερος — before, further; neut. comp. adv. προτέρω: ’further in’
προτὶ: πρός (epic by-form προτί) — towards, to; prep. + acc.
πρὸ: πρό — before, in front; prep. + gen.; also adv. or preverb in tmesis, ’ahead, forward’ (πρὸ … ἔαξεν ’broke ahead’)
πρῶτ: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially, elided (πρῶτ’ = πρῶτα): ’first’
πτολίεθρον: πτολίεθρον — citadel, city; neut. acc. sg., epic lengthened by-form of πόλις
πυθέσθαι: πυνθάνομαι — inquire, learn, hear of; aor. inf. mid. πυθέσθαι, epexegetic: ’to hear of’ (κλέος ... πυθέσθαι ’fame ... to hear of’)
πυθοίμην: πυνθάνομαι — learn, inquire; aor. opt. 1 sg. mid.
πως: πώς — somehow, in any way; enclitic adv. (οὔ πως ’in no way’)
πόδας: πούς — foot; acc. pl., accusative of respect
πόντον: πόντος — sea, open sea; acc. sg.
πόσιν: πόσις — husband; acc. sg. · also the distinct noun πόσις ’a drinking, drink’ (from πίνω); acc. sg.: ’drink’ (paired with βρῶσις ’eating’)
σιωπῇ: σιωπή — silence; fem. dat. sg., dative of manner: ’in silence’
σκοπιὴν: σκοπιή — lookout, watch-post; fem. acc. sg.: ’a watch’
στενάχοντα: στενάχω — groan, moan; pres. part. masc. acc. sg.: ’groaning’
σχεδὸν: σχεδόν — near, close by (+ gen.); adv. · also + dat.: σχεδὸν ἀλλήλῃσι ’close to one another’
σῖτον: σῖτος — bread, grain, the staple of a meal; acc. sg.
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’)
τέκε: τίκτω — bear, beget; aor. 3 sg., no augment (= ἔτεκε)
τέλεσ: τελέω — bring to an end, complete; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented, elided (τέλεσ’ = τέλεσε)
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. sg. · also the enclitic indefinite τις accented before a following enclitic, not interrogative: ’someone, anyone’ (ἤν τίς τοι εἴπῃσι ’if someone tells you’)
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τεῦχε: τεύχω — make, prepare, build; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔτευχε)
τινες: τις, τι — someone, something; masc. nom. pl. (after a relative, οἵ τινες = ὅστις pl.): ’whoever’ · also indefinite ’any’ after a negative: οὔ τινες ’not any, none’
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg.
τοὺς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. pl. ’them’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. pl. τοῖσιν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’from/to them’
τρίτατον: τρίτατος — third; epic superlative-form of τρίτος, masc. acc. sg.: ’as a third’
τρίτον: τρίτος — third; ordinal numeral, neut. nom. sg. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masc. noun: τρίτον ἄνδρα ’a third man’ (as direct object) · also neut. acc. sg., direct object: τρίτον ἦμαρ ’the third day’ (τέλεσ’ Ἠώς ’Dawn completed the third day’)
τότ: τότε — then, at that time; adv., elided (τότ’ = τότε)
τότε: τότε — then, at that time; adv.
τόφρα: τόφρα — so long, meanwhile; adv., correlative with ἕως ’until’
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’ · also ’it’, of a thing (τὴν = the clothing): fem. acc. sg. · also with a noun, article-like: τὴν ὁδόν ’that journey’
τὸ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg. (τὸ πάροιθεν ’that which was before’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’that, the’ (τὸ σῆμα ’that mark’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’)
τὼ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. dual: ’the two of them’  ·  also acc. dual, object of a verb of address: τὼ … προσέφη ’spoke to the two of them’ · also relative, nom. dual, ’who (the two)’: τοκῆε δύω, τὼ μὴ γείνασθαι ὄφελλον
τῶνδ: ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε — this, this one; masc. gen. pl., elided (τῶνδ’ = τῶνδε): ’of these’
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’) · also adverbial ’therefore, and so’ (τῷ οὔ τινα οἶδα ’so I know no one’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the same’ (ἤματι τῷ αὐτῷ ’on that same day’)
φέρων: φέρω — carry, bear; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’carrying’
φίλους: φίλος — dear, one’s own; substantival masc. acc. pl.: ’dear ones, kin’ · also adjective, ’dear’, agreeing with ἑταίρους
φαίνετο: φαίνω — show; mid. appear, seem; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἐφαίνετο)
φρένα: φρήν — mind, wits, heart; acc. sg. · also acc. of respect: ’in heart’ (γέγηθε φρένα ’is glad in heart’)
φρονέοντι: φρονέω — think, consider; pres. part. dat. sg. masc., agreeing with οἱ: ’to him as he considered’ · also agreeing with ἐμοί: ’to me as I thought’ (ἐμοὶ πυκινὰ φρονέοντι)
φύγοιμεν: φεύγω — flee, escape; aor. opt. 1 pl., in a purpose clause: ’that we might escape’
χάλκεον: χάλκεος — of bronze; masc./neut. acc. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic χαλκοῦν)
χθονὶ: χθών — earth, ground; fem. dat. sg.
χθονὸς: χθών — earth, ground; fem. gen. sg.
ἀέξετο: ἀέξω — make grow, increase; impf. pass. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἠέξετο): ’was growing’
ἀίοντες: ἀΐω — hear, perceive; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’hearing’, + gen.
ἀκαχήμενοι: ἀχέω (also ἀκαχίζω) — grieve, distress; perf. mid. part. masc. nom. pl., epic reduplicated: ’grieved’
ἀκταὶ: ἀκτή — shore, headland; fem. nom. pl.
ἀκτῆς: ἀκτή — grain, meal (a distinct epic word, homonym of ἀκτή ’shore’); gen. sg. · also ἀκτή ’shore, headland’, fem. gen. sg. (ἐπ’ ἀκτῆς ’on the shore’)
ἀλεγεινῆς: ἀλεγεινός — painful, grievous; fem. gen. sg.
ἀλλήλῃσιν: ἀλλήλων — one another; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι(ν)
ἀμφιελίσσας: ἀμφιέλισσα — curved at both ends (standing epithet of ships); fem. acc. pl.
ἀμφιελίσσης: ἀμφιέλισσα — curved on both sides, well-rounded (of a ship; sense debated); fem. gen. sg.
ἀμφοτέρωθεν: ἀμφότερος — both; adv. with suffix -θεν: ’on both sides’
ἀμφὶ: ἀμφί — on both sides, around, about; prep./adv. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἀμφὶ ... βάλλομεν = ἀμφιβάλλομεν ’we threw around, embraced’)
ἀνάσσοι: ἀνάσσω — be lord of, rule over (+ dat.); pres. opt. 3 sg.
ἀνέρες: ἀνήρ — man; masc. nom. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἄνδρες)
ἀολλέες: ἀολλής — all together, in a body; masc. nom. pl.
ἀπὸ: ἀπό — from, away from; + gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, separated from its verb (ἀπὸ … ὀλέσσει = ἀπολέσει ’will destroy’; ἀπὸ … δοθείη = ἀποδοθείη ’be given back’)
ἀσπασίως: ἀσπάσιος — glad, welcome; adv. ἀσπασίως: ’gladly, joyfully’
ἀφ: ἀπό — from, away from; prep. + gen., elided and aspirated before a rough breathing (ἀφ’ = ἀπό)
ἀφικόμεθ: ἀφικνέομαι — arrive, reach; aor. mid. 1 pl., elided (ἀφικόμεθ’ = ἀφικόμεθα): ‘we reached’
ἄλγεσι: ἄλγος — pain, grief; neut. dat. pl.
ἄλλαι: ἄλλος — other, another; fem. nom. pl.
ἄλλοθεν: ἄλλοθεν — from elsewhere, from another place; adv. (ἄλλος + -θεν ’from’)
ἄλλος: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. sg.
ἄμφω: ἄμφω — both; dual pron./adj., used with a dual verb · also with a plural noun: ἄμφω χεῖρας ’both hands’
ἄνδρε: ἀνήρ — man; masc. nom. dual: ’two men’
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, elided form ἄρ’ before a vowel · also the shortened form ἄρ used, without true elision, before τε in the fixed collocation ἄρ τε: τὰ μὲν ἄρ τε διεσκέδασ’
ἄσμενοι: ἄσμενος — glad, well pleased; masc. nom. pl.
ἄστεος: ἄστυ — city, town; neut. gen. sg.
ἄστυ: ἄστυ — town, city; neut. acc. sg.
ἅλα: ἅλς — sea, salt sea; fem. acc. sg.
ἅμ: ἅμα (elided ἅμ’) — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἅμα: ἅμα — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἐγὼν: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg., form used before a vowel
ἐείσατο: εἴδομαι — seem, appear; aor. 3 sg. ἐείσατο, unaugmented: ’seemed’
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐκβαίνοντα: ἐκβαίνω — step out, disembark; pres. part. acc. sg. masc., agreeing with an understood ’me’ (μ’ ἐκβαίνοντα)
ἐλθόντ: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. part. masc. acc. sg., elided (ἐλθόντ’ = ἐλθόντα): ’at his coming’
ἐμή: ἐμός — my, mine; fem. nom. sg.
ἐμήσατο: μήδομαι — devise, plan, contrive; aor. 3 sg.: ’contrived’
ἐμβαλέειν: ἐμβάλλω — throw in, cast upon; aor. inf. act., epic -έειν (= Attic ἐμβαλεῖν): ’to throw on’
ἐμοῖς: ἐμός — my, mine; masc. dat. pl.
ἐμὸν: ἐμός — my, mine; masc./neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject: ’my’ (ὄνομ’ … ἐμὸν ’my name’; ἐμὸν κῆρ ’my heart’)
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐοικότες: ἔοικα — be like, be fitting, resemble; perf. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’fitting’ (μῦθοι ἐοικότες ’fitting words’)
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’)
ἐπέεσσι: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic ἔπεσι)
ἐποτρύνας: ἐποτρύνω (also ὀτρύνω) — urge on, spur; aor. part. masc. nom. sg., + dat.: ’having roused (his comrades)’
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’) · also + dat., ’beyond, over and above, more than’ (ἐπὶ γαστέρι κύντερον ’more shameless than the belly’)
ἐρέοντο: ἐρέομαι — ask, inquire (often with ἐκ in tmesis, = ἐξερέοντο); impf. 3 pl. mid.: ’they asked’
ἐρυσσάμενος: ἐρύω — draw, drag, haul; aor. part. mid. masc. nom. sg., of launching a ship: ’having drawn down, having launched’ · also of a sword, ’drawing (from the sheath)’: ξίφος ὀξὺ ἐρυσσάμενος ’having drawn a sharp sword’
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐσχατιῇ: ἐσχατιή — the furthest point, edge, border; dat. sg.
ἐυπλόκαμος: ἐϋπλόκαμος — fair-tressed, with fine hair; fem. nom. sg. (Calypso’s standing epithet) · also used of Demeter (5.125), so not unique to Calypso despite the parenthetical above · also of Dawn (ἐυπλόκαμος Ἠώς ’fine-plaited Dawn’)
ἐόντα: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc./neut. acc. sg., epic (= Attic ὄντα)
ἑλὼν: αἱρέω — take, seize, grasp; aor. act. part. masc. nom. sg. (ἑλών): ’having seized’
ἑτάροισιν: ἕταρος — companion (by-form of ἑταῖρος); masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν
ἑτάρους: ἕταρος — companion (by-form of ἑταῖρος); acc. pl.
ἑτάρων: ἑταῖρος (epic ἕταρος) — companion, comrade; masc. gen. pl. (= Attic ἑταίρων)
ἑτέρῃ: ἕτερος — the other (of two); fem. dat. sg., often with χειρί understood: ’with the other (hand)’
ἑταίροισιν: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= -οις)
ἑταίρους: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. acc. pl.
ἔβαλον: βάλλω — throw, cast, put down; aor. 3 pl., augmented: ’they threw down’
ἔδοντες: ἔδω — eat (epic, = Attic ἐσθίω); pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’eating’
ἔκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; prep. + gen., placed after its pronoun with anastrophe: τοῦ ... ἔκ = ἐκ τοῦ ’from him’ · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἔκ … ὀνόμαζε = ἐξωνόμαζε ’called by name’)
ἔναιε: ναίω — dwell, inhabit, live; impf. 3 sg., augmented: ’was dwelling, lived’
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also used relatively, continuing a clause: ’where’ (ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’)
ἔνθεν: ἔνθεν — from there, thence; adv. of place, with suffix -θεν
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἔχεν: ἔχω — have, hold; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= εἶχεν): ’held’
ἔχον: ἔχω — have, hold, keep to; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented (= εἶχον) · also impf. 1 sg., unaugmented (= εἶχον): ’I had, I was carrying’
ἕκαστον: ἕκαστος — each, every; masc. acc. sg.
ἕνα: εἷς, μία, ἕν — one; masc. acc. sg. (ἕνα θυμόν ’one mind’)
ἠελίοιο: Ἠέλιος — the Sun (god); gen. sg., epic (-οιο = Attic Ἡλίου)
ἠώς: ἠώς — dawn; fem. nom. sg. (personified Ἠώς, Attic Ἕως)
ἡ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. sg.: ’she’
ἡγεμόνευεν: ἡγεμονεύω — lead the way, guide; impf. 3 sg.
ἤλθομεν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. 1 pl.: ’we came’
ἤματα: ἦμαρ — day; neut. acc. pl., acc. of time: ’all the days, every day’
ἦα: εἰμί — be; impf. 1 sg., epic ἦα (= Attic ἦν)
ἦεν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἦμαρ: ἦμαρ — day (epic for ἡμέρα); neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἧκεν: ἵημι — send, let go, put; aor. 3 sg. (ἧκα, with ν-movable; Attic ἧκε): ’sent, put’
ἰφθίμῃ: Ἰφθίμη — Iphthime, Penelope’s sister, wife of Eumelus; fem. dat. sg.
ἰόντας: εἶμι — go; pres. part. masc. acc. pl.: ’going’
ἱκέσθην: ἱκνέομαι — come to, arrive at, reach; aor. 3 dual
ἱκόμεσθα: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive; aor. 1 pl. mid., epic -μεσθα (= Attic -μεθα): ’we came’
ἴδοιμι: ὁράω — see; aor. 2 opt. 1 sg. (from εἶδον), in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’that I might see’
ἴδον: ὁράω — see; aor. 1 sg., unaugmented, from the root of εἶδον (= εἶδον) · also aor. 3 pl. (the same ending serves both persons): ’they saw’
ἴσαν: εἶμι — go, come; impf. 3 pl., epic: ’used to go, come’ · also as a simple narrative past, ’went’ (μνηστῆρες … ἴσαν ’the suitors went’), not necessarily iterative · also οἶδα — know; unaugmented plup. 3 pl. with impf. sense, epic (= Attic ᾔδεσαν): ’they knew’ (τὰ δ’ οὐκ ἴσαν ’they did not know’)
ἵν: ἵνα — so that, in order that; conj., elided (ἵν’ = ἵνα) · also relative adverb of place, ’where’ (= Attic οὗ): τῶν ἐνὶ δήμῳ, ἵν’ οἴχεται ’among those of the land where he has gone’
ὀλέσαντες: ὄλλυμι — destroy, lose; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having lost’
ὀλίγον: ὀλίγος — small, little, slight; masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.
ὀλοφύρατο: ὀλοφύρομαι — lament, pity, feel compassion for; aor. 3 sg. mid.
ὀλοόφρονος: ὀλοόφρων — baleful-minded (sense of this epithet, e.g. for Atlas, is debated; perhaps ’all-knowing’); gen. sg.
ὀξὺ: ὀξύς — sharp, keen; neut. acc. sg.
ὀπάσσας: ὀπάζω — send along as attendant, add; aor. part. masc. nom. sg., epic -σσ-: ’having added’
ὀρέων: ὄρος — mountain; neut. gen. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ὀρῶν)
ὀρώρει: ὄρνυμι — rouse; (intrans.) arise, spring up; pluperf. 3 sg., unaugmented: ’had sprung up’
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg.
ὁδόν: ὁδός — road, way, journey; fem. acc. sg.
ὁδὸν: ὁδός — way, journey; fem. acc. sg.
ὁμοῦ: ὁμοῦ — together, together with, at the same place; adv.
ὁμῶς: ὁμῶς — alike, in like manner, equally; adv.
ὃν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc./neut. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (masc. acc. sg.)
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄλεθρον: ὄλεθρος — destruction, ruin, death; acc. sg.
ὄλοντο: ὄλλυμι — destroy; mid. perish, be destroyed; aor. 3 pl. mid., no augment
ὄργυιαν: ὄργυια — fathom, arm-span (about six feet); fem. acc. sg., of extent
ὄφρ: ὄφρα (elided ὄφρ’) — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’as long as, while’ + indicative (ὄφρ’ ἔτι κεῖνος ἀνὴρ ἐπιδήμιος ἦεν ’as long as that man was still at home’) · also ’while’ + ἄν and subj. · also temporal ’until’ + indicative (ὄφρ’ ἵκετ’ Ἀρήτην ’until he came to Arete’) · also ’until’ + ἄν and subj. (ὄφρ’ ἂν ἵκηαι ’until you reach’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a secondary verb: ’so that … might’ (ὄφρ’ … μένοιεν)
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also with τις, an indirect interrogative: οὐκ οἶδ’ ὅς τις ’I know not who’ · also with τις, indefinite relative: ὅς τις … φάγοι ’whoever should eat’
ὅσον: ὅσος — as much as, as many as; masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.; neut. often adverbial: ’as much as’
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’) · also with the subjunctive, general: ’whenever’ (ὅτε στείχῃσ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’whenever she goes through the town’)
ὑπ: ὑπό (elided ὑπ’) — under, beneath; prep. + gen.; also + acc., ’under, up under’ · also of agent with a verb of dying, ‘by, at the hands of’ + gen. (ὤλεθ’ ὑπ’ Αἰγίσθοιο ‘perished by Aegisthus’) · also + dat., ’under, beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb, no case governed: οὓς ὑπ’ Ὀδυσσεὺς δύσετ’ = ὑπεδύσετο ’underneath which Odysseus sank down’
ὑπὲκ: ὑπέκ — out from under, forth from beneath; prep. + acc.; here in tmesis with φύγοιμεν: ’flee out from under’ (ὑπὲκ κακότητα φύγοιμεν)
ὑψηλῶν: ὑψηλός — high, lofty; masc./neut. gen. pl.
ὕδωρ: ὕδωρ — water; neut. acc. sg. · also nom. sg. (identical neut. form), subject of a verb (ἄνεμός τε καὶ ὕδωρ ‘wind and current’)
ὕλην: ὕλη — wood, timber, brushwood; fem. acc. sg.
ὕλης: ὕλη — wood, forest, thicket; fem. gen. sg.
ὠκεανὸς: Ὠκεανός — Oceanus, the river encircling the world; masc. nom. sg.
ὡπλίσσατο: ὁπλίζω — make ready, prepare, equip; aor. 3 sg. mid., epic double σ (ὡπλίσσατο): ’made ready for himself’
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὧδε: ὧδε — here, to this place, in this way; adv.
ᾗ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. dat. sg.: ’for which, to which’ (referring back to the ship, νηῦς) · also ’on which’, of a road: τὴν ὁδὸν ᾗ δὴ ’the journey on which’ · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: ’his own’, fem. dat. sg., agreeing with ἀλόχῳ (ᾗ … ἀλόχῳ ’his own wife’)
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥά: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, weak enclitic form ῥα, accented ῥά
